subject: Follow-up: Prompt/output data handling & retention — MedPulse
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@medpulse.com>, Tom Baker <tom.baker@medpulse.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: Prompt/output data handling & retention — MedPulse

Hi Elena / Tom,

Thanks again for the time this morning — great conversation and helpful context on how MedPulse routes clinician notes into your triage workflows. Per your ask, I wanted to capture a concise summary of what we can commit to today regarding prompt and output handling, and list concrete next steps.

High-level answers (tl;dr):
- What Redwood stores: for hosted customers we persist request metadata and a transient copy of prompt/response for up to 30 days by default; explicit PII can be configured not to be stored.
- Storage location: customer-controlled region selection (US, EU). For MedPulse we recommend US-WEST by default.
- Retention & exports: configurable retention windows; exports available via secure job (S3 presigned) or APIs.

Notes from the call (more detail):
1) Data types you send: you indicated clinician notes + structured EHR fields (patient name, MRN, DOB). We recommend pre-processing to tokenize/replace direct identifiers where possible before sending.
2) PII handling options: 
   - On-hosted API: default 30-day transient retention for prompt/outputs for debugging and quality monitoring. Can opt-in to 0-day retention for prompt/output storage; diagnostic logs still captured but redacted.
   - Private deployment (VPC/on-prem): complete control — no prompt/output leaves your network unless you choose.
3) Logging controls: request-level audit logs with retention policy; ability to disable full-text storage and retain only hashes/metadata for billing/metrics.
4) Residency: we can pin data and compute to US-WEST region; SOC2 and HIPAA addendum options available via contract.

Action items (ownership):
- Ben: share short whitepaper on prompt/output options + our recommended MAP for MedPulse (attached). (Today)
- Marissa: scope a short demo of redaction middleware and show preprocessing suggestions. (By 12/4)
- Rishi: confirm exact artifact set available for SOC2/HIPAA review (logs, retention configs). (By 12/2)
- Elena/Tom: confirm whether you want default 30-day storage for troubleshooting or 0-day redaction-first approach. (Reply)

Attachments: redwood-prompt-data-whitepaper.pdf (overview), medpulse-map.json (recommended config map)

If that looks right I’ll loop in contracts once you confirm the residency/retention preference and we’ll provision a short trial configuration.

Thanks,
Ben

Ben — thanks for the summary. This is very helpful. Quick clarifications from our side before we pick a retention policy: 

1) When you say "transient copy of prompt/response for up to 30 days" — is that full text available to anyone at Redwood, or access-controlled? We need to ensure only designated SRE/security personnel can request access.
2) For the redaction option (0-day storage), can the system still keep identifiers hashed for deduplication/metrics without retaining raw text?
3) If we go hosted but want HIPAA, is there a BAA template or steps you can share now?

Tom is looped in to confirm the compliance/legal asks. We are leaning toward 0-day storage for prompt/outputs in the pilot, with retention of minimal metadata (hashes, model id, timestamp). Can you confirm whether that will impact debugging capabilities for the pilot?

Best,
Elena

elena@medpulse.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 08:31:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Prompt/output data handling & retention — MedPulse

Hi Elena — quick answers to your numbered questions below. I’ve pasted the most relevant engineering/controls info so your legal/compliance folks can see the exact artifacts we surface.

1) Access controls: Full-text stored prompt/outputs are encrypted at rest with customer-key option (KMS); access is role-based and logged. Only personnel with the "security:incident" or "sre:debug" roles can request a job to view raw text; such requests require an approval workflow and are recorded in the audit log with justification.

2) Hashing: Yes — we can store deterministic hashes (SHA-256) for prompt/response tokens or whole-payload to support dedup and metrics without retaining raw text. Hashes are one-way and cannot be reversed to plaintext. This is how we implement 0-day-mode for hosted customers: raw text is redacted immediately and only hashes/metadata retained for X days.

3) BAA/Compliance artifacts: We maintain a standard BAA and SOC2 artifacts. I attached a short SOC2 evidence summary (SOC2-evidence-summary.pdf) in this thread. For HIPAA pilot we can run under our standard BAA and enable Business Associate controls (audit retention windows, KMS in customer region).

Impacts to debugging (tradeoffs):
- 30-day full-text helps reproduce incidents quickly; with 0-day/redaction you lose the immediate ability to replay an exact conversation. We mitigate this by: 
  a) longer retention of structured logs and model inputs (with identifiers hashed),
  b) dev-mode sampling (with customer consent) to retain a tiny fraction (e.g., 0.1%) of full-text for postmortems, and
  c) on-demand ephemeral replay where customers can opt-in to store a trace for a specific session for N days.

If you want, we can produce a one-page comparison table for MedPulse that lists operational impact vs. privacy posture.

-Rishi
Head of Security | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Prompt/output data handling & retention — MedPulse

Elena / Tom — thanks for the questions and Rishi for the detailed answers. To keep momentum, proposed pilot configuration below (please confirm):

Pilot configuration (recommended):
- Deployment: Hosted API in US-WEST region
- Prompt/output handling: 0-day redaction-first (raw text redacted on ingestion)
- Metadata retained: deterministic hashes (SHA-256), model id, timestamp, token counts, error codes
- Debugging: enable dev-mode sampling (0.1% full-text kept, customer opt-in via portal)
- Audit & access: KMS-managed keys (customer-managed), RBAC enforced, approver workflow for any raw-text access
- Compliance: run under standard BAA; we will share the contract draft upon confirmation

Next steps: 
- Elena: confirm you agree with the pilot config above and whether to proceed with 0.1% sampling (Y/N).
- Marissa: schedule a 30-min demo of the redaction middleware for the integration team (owner: marissa).
- Rishi: handoff SOC2 artifacts to MedPulse legal (owner: rishi).
- Ben: open a HubSpot task and provision pilot keys once decision is confirmed.

I’ve attached the whitepaper and the recommended config map for the pilot. If that matches your expectations I’ll ask contracts to send a pilot addendum and we’ll have the trial environment ready within 48 hours of getting the signed addendum.

–Ben
